ctx.x: What I talk about is only hearsay, which perhaps shouldn't be talked about, but I wrote a little piece in my first book about, I say, in defense of Benny Goodman, that when one hears the pernicious things he is supposed to have done, one readily wants to hate him, but Benny Goodman came in to the Roosevelt Hotel about six years ago when I was playing with the World's Greatest Jazz Band and he was absolutely charming, you know, just another guy, that but I never knew.
And another thing about him, Bud, do you know he goes to -- I mean, when people go, Benny is there at that service. Billy Strayhorn, no matter who. I mean, if he's known them, he's there.
If there is something to hear in music,
